issues.description: Method signature mismatch for SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery: The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplierName: String, ingredientName: String, price: int, quantity: int). The solution implementation and the example usage in the template (Main.java) use a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (ingredient name, price, quantity) with no supplier parameter. This discrepancy leaves students unsure which signature to implement and may cause tests or example calls to fail if they follow the problem statement instead of the template/solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration consistent across artifacts. Preferred: update the problem statement to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (i.e., remove the supplierName parameter) to match the existing template usage and solution. Alternatively, if retaining the supplier parameter is required for pedagogical reasons, update the template Main.java example and the solution SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery signature/implementation to accept four parameters: acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity), and adjust all calls accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies a SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery method that takes four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) e.g. acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). However, the template/solution implement and call a three-parameter method acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) where the single String parameter is the ingredient name. This mismatch between the required signature in the problem statement and the actual method in the template/solution makes it unclear which parameters students must implement and whether a supplierName parameter is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across artifacts. Preferred: update the template and solution to use the four-parameter signature public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (and update calls in Main to include a supplierName). Alternatively, if supplierName is intentionally irrelevant, update the problem statement and UML to require the three-parameter signature public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity).
